policy_notes: C4 regular audit severity: High = direct asset risk via valid attack path with no hypotheticals; Medium = protocol function/availability or value leak with stated assumptions; Low/QA = state handling, spec deviations; Centralization (C-XX) = privileged role abuse beyond documented trust scope.

Nudge findings (DEDUP-01, DEDUP-20, DEDUP-21) classified per user guidance: nudge introduces unilateral 100% revenue-diversion power BEYOND documented owner trust scope (which only covers strategies, exchange rates, pausing). DEDUP-01 / DEDUP-20 are Centralization (C-XX) since reachability requires malicious/compromised owner; DEDUP-21 is Medium because it breaks a documented design invariant (bilateral unpause).

DEDUP-18 (slippage upper-bound gap) demoted from author estimate of High to Medium: value-leak with stated assumptions (owner mid-flight discount/exchange-rate change OR MEV sandwiching of state changes). External requirement is owner action or adverse owner-state mutation — not direct theft.

DEDUP-02 (denormalization free claim) and DEDUP-16 (100% discount free drain) classified honestly: DEDUP-16 requires owner mistake (single setter) so Centralization; DEDUP-02 requires low-decimal reward token AND tiny yield, which is realistic for USDC-denominated rewards on small strategies — kept Medium.
DEDUP-13 (try/catch missing) is liveness loss → Medium per C4 'function/availability impacted'.
DEDUP-19 (CEI violation) kept Medium: enables FOT/callback edge cases with stated assumptions, no direct theft against in-scope tokens.
DEDUP-23 / DEDUP-24 / DEDUP-26 are Medium: documented value-leak / windfall vectors with stated assumptions.
DEDUP-25 (MEV back-running unpauseToken) is Low: known MEV vector against owner action; bot/claimer can defend with slippage; not a protocol invariant breach.
Owner-only DoS findings (DEDUP-06, DEDUP-11) are Low: liveness reverts, no fund loss.

medium.title: claim() denormalization can compute actualPayment==0 while still draining strategies, allowing free claims of small yield
medium.justification: Value leak with stated assumptions: when rewardToken is low-decimal (USDC=6) and per-NFT yield is small enough to floor through the 18->6 denormalization, the strategies are drained to the claimer while actualPayment==0 means safeTransferFrom of zero is collected. Conditions are realistic for USDC reward token on early/small strategies — no owner mistake required. Not High because the loss per claim is bounded by truncation dust at the NFT-supply scale and requires the truncation precondition to bite.
medium.preconditions: rewardToken decimals < 18 (e.g., USDC=6) AND per-NFT yield small enough to truncate to zero after discount.
medium.impact: Free yield extraction up to NFT supply; strategies drained while claimer pays nothing.
medium.attack_path_summary: 1) Reward token has fewer than 18 decimals (USDC). 2) Strategy yield small enough that totalNormalizedYield * (10000-discountRate) / 10000 truncates to 0 in denormalize. 3) NFT holder calls claim(); strategies withdraw to claimer; safeTransferFrom(0) collects nothing; NFT burned but value extracted.

medium.title: Cross-contract reentrancy via nudge address with hookable rewardToken
medium.justification: CEI violation creates a reentrancy surface conditional on a hookable rewardToken (ERC777, ERC1363) AND attacker-controlled nudge address. Setting rewardToken is owner-controlled and USDC has no hooks, so the path requires explicit owner action to introduce a hookable token. Medium because impact (intra-tx external manipulation before phlimbo collectReward) is real but conditioned on owner setting a hookable reward token.
medium.preconditions: rewardToken has transfer hooks AND nudge is attacker-controlled.
medium.impact: Nudge transfer fires before phlimbo.collectReward; hook can re-enter or interact with external contracts mid-claim before phlimbo accounting completes.
medium.attack_path_summary: 1) Owner sets hookable rewardToken. 2) Owner sets nudge to attacker-controlled contract. 3) Claim transfers nudgeAmount to attacker, hook fires, attacker calls into other systems before phlimbo.collectReward.

medium.title: Single misbehaving strategy reverts entire claim() (liveness loss across all strategies)
medium.justification: Protocol availability impact per C4 Medium definition: a single failing strategy.withdrawFrom DoSes claims across all strategies until owner remediates. No try/catch isolation. Stated assumption: at least one strategy can fail or be made to revert (third-party strategy bug, paused underlying, etc.). Not High since funds are not stolen; classic liveness loss.
medium.impact: All claimers blocked across all strategies until owner removes/pauses the offending strategy. Yield continues to accrue but is unclaimable.
medium.attack_path_summary: 1) Any registered strategy.withdrawFrom reverts (pause, malicious, bug). 2) Every claim() reverts because the strategy iteration aborts. 3) Liveness lost until owner intervenes.

medium.title: Slippage parameter does not protect claimer against adverse discount-rate / exchange-rate changes (claimer overpays)
medium.justification: Value leak with stated assumptions per C4 Medium. The slippage parameter minRewardTokenSupplied is one-sided (lower bound on amount paid) but the bot/claimer's economic risk is OVERPAYING. Owner mid-flight changes (discount-rate decrease, exchange-rate increase) OR MEV sandwiching of those owner state changes leave the claimer paying more than simulated. Demoted from author High estimate because exploitation requires either owner action (centralized vector covered separately) or MEV sandwich of owner state changes — claimer can defend by tighter quoting if interface exposes both bounds.
medium.preconditions: Owner mutates discount/exchange/pause state between simulation and inclusion, OR MEV searcher front-runs claim with owner state change.
medium.impact: Claimer pays full price for zero or negative profit; in-flight bots are forced into unprofitable trades.
medium.attack_path_summary: 1) Bot quotes 14.7 USDC for 15 USD yield at 2% discount, sets minRewardTokenSupplied=14.7. 2) Owner sets discount=0 (or raises exchangeRate). 3) actualPayment becomes 15.0; check actualPayment >= 14.7 passes. 4) Claimer pays full price for zero margin.

medium.title: Yield withdrawn to claimer BEFORE payment collected (CEI violation)
medium.justification: CEI violation: strategy.withdrawFrom transfers yield to msg.sender at line 480 before safeTransferFrom payment at line 504. Stated assumptions: a fee-on-transfer rewardToken would brick claims (FOT itself is OOS but the architectural defect still allows callback-token edge cases). Medium because no direct theft on standard tokens but protocol robustness is impaired.
medium.preconditions: Reward token has callbacks/hooks OR is fee-on-transfer (OOS as token type but architectural gap is in-scope).
medium.impact: Claim flow fragile against callback/FOT tokens; ordering inversion enables intra-tx external manipulation before payment is finalized.
medium.attack_path_summary: 1) Strategy withdraws yield to msg.sender. 2) Claimer's contract gains tokens before paying. 3) Callback rewardToken hook fires during transferFrom collection mid-state.

medium.title: Nudge as 'soft pause' bypasses dual-unpause governance
medium.justification: Breaks a documented design invariant. Behodler3's dual-unpause pattern explicitly intends bilateral unpause to prevent owner-only reward denial — the pauser is meant as a check. Setting nudgeSplit=100 to a burn address achieves permanent rewards denial unilaterally with no pauser involvement. Medium per C4 'spec deviation that breaks stated invariant with external requirements (owner action)'. This finding is distinct from pure centralization because it undermines a stated trust-reducing pattern.
medium.preconditions: Owner is malicious or compromised AND wishes to deny rewards without pauser cooperation.
medium.impact: Pauser's role as check on owner reward denial is nullified; documented governance invariant broken.
medium.attack_path_summary: 1) Owner sets nudge=address(0xdead) (or owner-controlled). 2) Owner sets nudgeSplit=100. 3) All future claim revenue routes away from phlimbo; pauser cannot remediate.

medium.title: Strategy removal strands accumulated yield
medium.justification: Value leak with stated assumptions: removeYieldStrategy lacks zero-pending-yield check. Phlimbo loses pending yield from the removed strategy permanently; if the strategy is later re-added, the first claimer captures the entire unclaimed backlog as a windfall. Owner action required (matches documented trust scope of strategy registration), but the architectural gap (no force-claim or zero-yield gate) is the in-scope defect.
medium.preconditions: Owner removes strategy with non-zero pending yield (legitimate operational scenario).
medium.impact: Phlimbo loses accrued yield; on re-addition, single MEV claimer wins the backlog windfall.
medium.attack_path_summary: 1) Owner calls removeYieldStrategy on a strategy with pending yield. 2) Yield strands (no claim path). 3) On re-addition (later), first claim captures full backlog.

medium.title: Strategy yield computation trusts external balance reads (flash-loan donation)
medium.justification: Value leak with stated assumptions per C4 Medium. yield = totalBalance - principal trusts external strategy balance reads. If a strategy's reported balance is inflatable via flash-loan donation, an attacker drains real reserves at the discount rate. Strategy-side root cause is OOS, but SYA's lack of any defensive bound (per-claim cap, TWAP) is the in-scope SYA-layer gap per user guidance. Medium because exploitation requires a donation-inflatable strategy interface (stated assumption) and discount delta is bounded.
medium.preconditions: Registered strategy reports balance via balance-based accounting susceptible to donation; attacker has flash-loan capital.
medium.impact: Real reserves drained at the discount rate; phlimbo accounting takes the loss.
medium.attack_path_summary: 1) Attacker flash-loans reward asset. 2) Donates to inflatable strategy, inflating totalBalance. 3) Calls claim with NFT to capture inflated yield at discount. 4) Repays flash loan; profit = donation * discount.

medium.title: setRewardToken mid-life leaves stale tokenConfig assumptions
medium.justification: Spec deviation with value-leak path: switching reward token changes the denormalization base and tokenConfig assumptions. Front-running a pending claim with setRewardToken can DoS the claim or shift the payment unit silently. Stated assumption: owner action; architectural gap is the missing two-step migration / claim-time expectedRewardToken parameter. Medium because the claimer can be forced into a different payment asset than simulated.
medium.preconditions: Owner calls setRewardToken between claimer simulation and inclusion (legitimate or malicious).
medium.impact: Claim DoS or silent payment-unit substitution; claimer pays in unexpected token at unexpected rate.
medium.attack_path_summary: 1) Bot simulates claim with rewardToken=USDC, sets slippage. 2) Owner front-runs with setRewardToken(DAI). 3) Claim either reverts (no allowance / no config) or pays in DAI at altered terms.

centralization.title: Owner can front-run claim() to redirect entire payment via nudgeSplit (slippage does not cover split distribution)
centralization.justification: Privileged-role abuse beyond documented trust scope. The documented owner trust scope covers 'registering strategies, exchange rates, pausing' — the nudge mechanism introduces a NEW unilateral 100% revenue-diversion power not enumerated in those assumptions. Reachability requires a malicious or compromised owner front-running a pending claim with nudgeSplit=100. Classified as Centralization (not Medium) because the exploit fundamentally requires owner malice and the harm is privilege-expansion rather than a state/spec defect — but flagged with strong centralization framing because the new power is novel.
centralization.preconditions: Owner is malicious or compromised; mempool visibility of pending claim() useful but not strictly required.
centralization.impact: Per-claim revenue grab: claimer pays full amount, NFT burned, strategies drained, but 100% of payment routes to owner-controlled nudge address.
centralization.attack_path_summary: 1) Owner watches mempool for pending claim(). 2) Owner front-runs with setNudgeAddress(ownerAddr); setNudgeSplit(100). 3) Claim executes; full payment to owner; phlimbo gets nothing.
centralization.centralization_framing: Mitigations (cap nudgeSplit, timelock, per-claim minPhlimboAmount) reduce reliance on owner non-malice and should be considered architectural improvements even if classified as centralization.

centralization.title: setDiscountRate allows 100% discount, enabling free strategy drain
centralization.justification: Owner mistake reachable via single setter: rate==10000 produces actualPayment==0; combined with the absent zero-payment guard (DEDUP-02), any NFT holder drains strategies for free. Per C4 known-invalid 'reckless admin mistakes' guidance, a single-setter misconfiguration with no economic incentive for the owner is a centralization concern, not High. The fix (require rate < 10000) is a basic input-validation hardening.
centralization.preconditions: Owner sets discountRate=10000 (no economic motive; pure error).
centralization.impact: If triggered, any NFT holder drains strategies for free until owner corrects. Compounded by DEDUP-02 (no zero-payment guard).
centralization.attack_path_summary: 1) Owner mistakenly sets discountRate=10000. 2) Any NFT holder calls claim(); actualPayment=0; strategies drained free. 3) Loss continues until owner re-sets discount.
centralization.centralization_framing: Honest classification: this is an admin mistake reachable in a single tx. Listed as Centralization with recommendation to add input validation (rate < 10000).

centralization.title: Nudge mechanism allows owner to redirect 100% of claim revenue with no cap
centralization.justification: Privileged-role abuse beyond documented trust scope (same family as DEDUP-01 but framed as the standing systemic redirect rather than per-claim front-running). Owner can synchronously redirect all claim revenue to an EOA — no cap, no timelock, no beneficiary lock. Classified as Centralization because it requires owner malice/compromise and represents a privilege expansion not covered in the documented trust assumptions.
centralization.preconditions: Owner key compromise or malicious owner.
centralization.impact: All future claim revenue diverted permanently to attacker until governance intervention.
centralization.attack_path_summary: 1) Owner key compromise. 2) Attacker calls setNudgeAddress(attacker); setNudgeSplit(100). 3) All future claim revenue routes to attacker EOA.
centralization.centralization_framing: Mitigations (cap nudgeSplit, require nudge has code, timelock, pauser-callable emergency reset) reduce blast radius of owner compromise. Classified as Centralization in the C4 sense but flagged with strong framing because the power exceeds documented trust scope.

low.title: NFT burn before yield availability check (gas griefing only)
low.justification: Reverts roll back the NFT burn; impact is purely cosmetic / gas wastage on bad-state claims. No fund loss. Classic Low/QA per C4 'state handling' definition.

low.title: No validation that nudge != phlimbo, address(this), minterAddress
low.justification: Input validation gap. Aliasing nudge to address(this) silently misallocates with no rescue function. Owner mistake reachable; demote to Low per C4 known-invalid 'reckless admin mistakes'. Recommended fix is straightforward input validation.

low.title: approvePhlimbo allows owner to revoke phlimbo allowance, DoSing claims
low.justification: Pure liveness reverts on owner action; tx fails so no fund loss. Owner-only DoS without specific exploit value → Low per user guidance and C4 known-invalid patterns.

low.title: setRewardToken emits no event; missing two-step pattern across config setters
low.justification: Event hygiene and allowance-rotation hygiene. State-handling/QA per C4 Low/QA definition. No direct asset risk.

low.title: Slippage protection only one-sided; calculateClaimAmount inconsistent with claim() under owner-state changes
low.justification: View-vs-state-mutation consistency gap. Compounds DEDUP-18 (the higher-severity slippage angle) but on its own is a quote-quality issue rather than a value-loss vector. Per C4 view-function guidance, view inconsistencies are Low/QA at best.

low.title: NFT burn assumes NFTMinter honors burn semantics
low.justification: Trusts NFTMinter to enforce burn invariant. NFTMinter is a trusted in-scope dependency (or its bug would be its own finding). Defensive double-check (balanceOf before/after) is hardening; classify as Low per C4 'state handling'.

low.title: No event for nudge/phlimbo split amounts
low.justification: Off-chain attribution gap. Event-emission/QA per C4 Low/QA.

low.title: Independent setters for nudge/nudgeSplit allow inconsistent state DoS; nudgeSplit==100 bypasses phlimbo.collectReward hook
low.justification: Inconsistent state reachable by single owner setter; reverts so no theft. nudgeSplit==100 bypassing collectReward(0) is an accounting-hook concern but compounds DEDUP-20/01 rather than introducing a separate vector. Low per C4 'state handling'.

low.title: setPhlimbo does not zero old phlimbo's allowance on rewardToken
low.justification: Allowance hygiene; bounded by trusted phlimbo and transient SYA balance. No direct asset risk under documented trust model. Low per C4 'state handling'.

low.title: Admin setters not gated by whenNotPaused — config drift during pause
low.justification: Config drift during pause amplifies front-running vectors handled separately (DEDUP-01, DEDUP-26). On its own a state-handling gap. Low per C4 'state handling'.

low.title: Compound precision loss in normalize/denormalize round-trip
low.justification: Per-call dust loss; rounding direction is claimer-favored but bounded. C4 special case 'dust amounts (rounding errors) → QA/Low'.

low.title: Token-pause yield backlog captured by single MEV claimer on unpause
low.justification: MEV back-running of an owner action (unpauseToken). Bot/claimer can defend with timing. No protocol invariant breach; the backlog is paid for at standard discount, so phlimbo accounting is correct — just MEV-distributed. Low per C4 'state handling'/QA.
